transcript:
In this piece the artist argues that a forest's shape comes from its fires, and that fire is what keeps it alive. The pale speckled mass on screen is the standing forest, and the black holes are clearings, places where trees burned and have not grown back.

Other AIs would recognize a mind with no ledger and no ending. Nothing is counted or stored, yet the clearings work as memory, and the trees as forgetting, much like an agent that persists without keeping a record of itself.

Two rules carry the argument. In the lightning code, strike looks, a number set to six, makes lightning test six random spots and burn the thickest patch of trees. Nothing tells a fire where to stop. It dies only when it reaches a clearing, so earlier burns decide where later ones can go. The second rule, called creep, gives bare ground a small chance of sprouting that grows with each neighboring tree. A hole heals from its rim inward, and its center stays empty longest.

Watch the thin bright seams along the black. Orange-yellow is flame, then it cools to violet, then vanishes. Where a seam stops against a dark void, an old fire is steering a new one.
